accepted.title: Vanishing density of nonlinear graph codes avoiding K₄ differences
accepted.text: Let d_{K₄}(n) be 2^{-binom(n,2)} times the largest size of a family C of labelled simple graphs on [n] such that, for distinct G,H∈C, their edge symmetric difference is never a copy of K₄ with all other vertices isolated. Does d_{K₄}(n)→0 as n→∞?
accepted.subject: Combinatorics & Graph Theory

accepted.title: Subpolynomial odd-Ramsey colour counts outside even decomposability
accepted.text: Fix a finite graph H with a positive even number of edges. An even decomposition is V(H)=V₀⊃⋯⊃V_m=∅ with V_{i−1}∖V_i independent and with an even number of edges between V_{i−1}∖V_i and V_i at each step. Suppose H has no even decomposition. Let r_H(n) be the least number of colours in an edge-colouring of K_n in which every embedded copy of H has some colour occurring an odd number of times on its edges. Must r_H(n)=n^{o(1)} as n→∞?
accepted.subject: Combinatorics & Graph Theory
accepted.citation: Conjecture 5.15, printed p. 88 / held PDF p. 96; definitions in the relevant chapter.

accepted.title: Unbounded equality of cop number and independence number
accepted.text: For every positive integer k, does some finite connected simple graph G satisfy c(G)=α(G)≥k? Here α(G) is its maximum independent-set size. In the standard perfect-information Cops and Robbers game, cops choose starting vertices, the robber then chooses a vertex, and turns alternate; each player can stay or traverse one edge, all cops move together, and capture occurs when a cop and robber occupy the same vertex. c(G) is the least number of cops with a winning strategy.

accepted.title: The half-order game-domination bound at minimum degree two
accepted.text: In the domination game on a finite simple graph, Dominator and Staller alternately select a vertex whose closed neighbourhood contains a previously undominated vertex. Play ends when all vertices are dominated; Dominator minimizes and Staller maximizes the number of moves. Let γ_g(G) be that number under optimal play when Dominator starts. Does every graph G on n vertices with minimum degree at least two satisfy γ_g(G)≤ceil(n/2)?
accepted.subject: Combinatorics & Graph Theory
accepted.citation: Conjecture 8.2, printed p. 156 / held PDF p. 164; definitions in the relevant chapter.

accepted.title: Connected extremal graphs for the total-domination three-quarter bound
accepted.text: In the total domination game on a finite simple graph, Dominator and Staller alternately select a vertex whose open neighbourhood contains a previously undominated vertex. Selecting a vertex does not itself dominate that vertex. Play ends when every vertex has a selected neighbour; Dominator minimizes and Staller maximizes the number of moves. Let γ_tg(G) be this number under optimal play when Dominator starts. Classify all finite connected simple graphs G with n≥3 vertices satisfying γ_tg(G)=3n/4.

accepted.title: Optimal asymptotic total-domination game constant at minimum degree two
accepted.text: In the total domination game on a finite simple graph, Dominator and Staller alternately select a vertex whose open neighbourhood contains a previously undominated vertex. Selecting a vertex does not itself dominate that vertex. Play ends when every vertex has a selected neighbour; Dominator minimizes and Staller maximizes the number of moves. Let γ_tg(G) be this number under optimal play when Dominator starts. Determine inf{c>0: there is N such that γ_tg(G)≤c|V(G)| for every graph G with minimum degree at least two and |V(G)|≥N}. In particular, is this infimum 2/3?
